reason: The opcodes, branch ranges and counts check out on the 65SC12: hot path 46 -> 35 cycles (11 saved), 30 -> 45 bytes (+15). The equivalence is still wrong. It assumes that right = left + 79 (mod 65536) makes D = left - x equal R - 79 with the same unsigned borrows. That fails whenever the 16-bit viewport wraps: left is &FFxx while right is &00xx. The game starts that way: reset_screen_scroll sets left &FFB0, right &FFFF, and the first right scroll makes right &0000 while left is still &FFB1. Observer mode (game.6502 observer_mode_loop) scrolls LEFT from column 0 with no bound, and each step renders (update_screen_observer -> update_screen). One LEFT from the start gives left = &FFFF, right = &004E. Take a mover at x = &0010. The old code finds left >= x unsigned, goes to left_of_view, D = &FFEF, high byte non-zero, so jmin = 255 (nothing visible): it is clipped. The new code finds R = &3E with no borrow, high byte 0 and Y < 79, so it stores jmin 0 and jmax &3E and draws the mover. So draw_mover behaves differently in a state the shipping build can reach (tools/observer.mjs drives LEFT). The window also grows 15 bytes and slides bank 4's later indexed table reads, which the candidate does not count.
